hook_text: Draw a perfect square corner with only a compass. No protractor.
clip_script: With a compass and ruler, to construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment AB: open the compass to more than half of AB. With the point on A, draw an arc above and below AB. Keep the same opening, put the point on B, and draw arcs crossing the first two. Join the two crossing points with a ruler. This line is perpendicular to AB and passes through its midpoint.
visual_style: A compass sweeps two arcs from A and two from B; the crossing points glow and a ruler joins them; a right-angle square pops at the midpoint.
pacing: Steady arc sweeps, pause on crossings, snap the line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to construct any angle and parallel lines too.
